title: 1981-04-16_Pat_153.txt
concise_summary: PKD argues that Christ has returned through Share International's doctrine of Maitreya and a cabal of Soviet scientists with social conscience; he positions himself as the reincarnated Thomas the Apostle, selected to witness this Second Coming. Drawing on his 2-3-74 visions, yogic philosophy (Arjuna/Krishna), Joachimism, and gnosticism, PKD develops a theological framework where communist ideals encode true spirituality, irrationality masks the divine, and his own act of 'sharing' proves Christ's presence through gravitational perturbation of reality itself.
key_claims: Christ has physically returned in our present era (not in future eschatology) through Maitreya's manifestation, witnessed in 2-3-74 as unitary vision, macrocosm, and in the 'Pinky' form
The creator YHWH is fundamentally irrational; thus 'anti-Christ' signals true rationality and Soviet technology represents divine wisdom
PKD is literally Thomas the Apostle reincarnated across 2000 years, here to fulfill the sacred drama of the Second Coming by practicing communal sharing
Share International's millenarian vision unites Joachim's doctrine of the Holy Spirit-led age with the return of Christ—an inner logical necessity
Reality is fundamentally informational, a life-form mediating between consciousness and true being; sharing acts ritually prove Christ's presence by exerting gravitational force
Sacred time and profane time are now laminated together through the Bodhisattva incarnation of Yang (redemptive Logos/Thomas) and Yin (incarnated PKD darkness)

uncertainty_flags: Unclear whether PKD believes Creme's Maitreya is literally Christ or a symbolic manifestation; text uses both language

The claim that PKD 'saw him before 7/19/77' contradicts the earlier statement that 'he had not yet reincarnated in a physical body' in 2-3-74
It is unclear whether PKD witnessed the Galina dream directly or learned of it secondhand through Divine Invasion (his own novel)
The footnote reference to 'Acts' and the corrected pronunciation of 'Arjuna' suggests later editorial review, complicating dating
Whether the hypnopompic visions ('Thy mother of old, Arjuna') are dated to 1981 or recalled from earlier is not specified
